# D175 — Select bounded plugin observability diagnostics for #442

Authority: the owner delegated blocker decisions for this batch, with a catalogue of reasons and alternatives for consolidated review before owner QA. This is an agent-selected decision under that authority, not human plan approval or completed acceptance.

Select the sealed `i4-442-discovery-01/PLAN.md` (SHA-256 c67eb744b189e136713c959d49c97364a361a9ee489578e821e1a9e80c6833bc): a fixed shared domain readiness notice, a `plugins.codex` warning after successful Codex system preflight, and the same honest scope notice in the existing Codex Settings card. Actual Claude Code owns UI implementation, copy and component tests; GPT owns the pure notice/backend/tests/docs. The warning preserves readiness, authentication failures, exit status, Retry and the existing Settings query. It starts no provider, inventory or configuration probe and changes no plugin policy.

The wording must say loaded plugin tools are **not verified by this check**, not claim every supported CLI interface lacks diagnostics or declare a configured plugin broken. CLI list commands are useful inventory, not complete loaded-tool health proof. A generic preflight has no specific inference node's effective worker directory/overrides.

D174 outcome: all three bounded app-server containment attempts caused curated HTTPS Git fetching, including the supported remote_plugin=false experiment. Stop that lane; preserve every failure and cleanup record. No app-server integration is selected. CLI-only discovery separately completed two plugins-off controls and twelve distinct matrix continuation cases. The first healthy plugin control produced its actual tool/result and closed processes, but its direct exit observer was lost when the SDK removed listeners; preserve that original failed observer assertion instead of counting it as a fully observed native-exit pass. The original two aborted plugin turns remain termination-unconfirmed. Git fixtures used file transport, not remote authentication or service-health proof.

Alternatives declined: a new warnings schema expands contracts unnecessarily; overloading ready `problems` conflates scope with failure; app-server integration currently violates the bounded read-only probe requirement; private cache/manifest parsing creates a plugin manager and filesystem trust surface; automatically invoking arbitrary plugin services/tools can cause effects; disabling plugins changes accepted policy; documentation alone adds no diagnostic for operators of the existing preflight.

Independent review must cross model families for both backend and UI. Independent native/public/browser QA, current-target CI, existing coverage thresholds and final designated review remain open. #439 and owner acceptance remain open. No issue closure, installation or deployment is authorized by this record alone.

# D176 — Diagnose Claude process start refusals without false installation claims

Authority: owner-delegated blocker decisions, subject to the consolidated decision catalogue and owner QA. Source candidate is 99f1de7863dfc6a05b63a9140f7fc7a6833fcb20, tree 911b2400b7622b5b04b58b3b03092d9ea90f55a3, based on 02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c. Actual Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh implemented it; this record is not independent approval.

Select bounded, post-refusal diagnostics only when no child PID was assigned. A proved missing absolute executable remains HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED and restorable. A missing or non-directory turn working directory is HARNESS_INVALID_CONFIGURATION and pinned non-resumable. An ambiguous start refusal stays HARNESS_TURN_FAILED/unknown and does not assert a missing executable. A read-only stat failure cannot prove an existing directory startable. The Windows long-path fact may be mentioned as a limit without declaring it the proven cause. No PATH resolver, fallback command or trial launch is added.

Cancellation/deadline during the diagnostic settles without waiting for stat or inventing a timeout. Proven refusal remains definitely-not-started; termination/abort precedence is preserved. Native probing also exposed ENOTCONN on pipes for a never-started long-path child. Include guarded pipe error handling at this same process boundary: ignore a never-started child's pipe failure, but treat a started child's output loss as potentially hiding acceptance and terminate its owned process tree. Do not downgrade output loss to a safe refusal based on later stderr.

Alternatives declined: map every ENOENT to missing CLI (demonstrably false for existing binaries with invalid cwd); mark every existing cwd startable (Windows native evidence contradicts it); retry or fallback (could repeat effects); global path/environment changes (affect concurrent work); omit pipe error handling (native reproducer can crash the process); broadly change other process adapters based only on similar source (requires separate evidence and scope).

Author evidence includes the native baseline, focused tests, mutation checks and scoped Claude-folder coverage. The full infrastructure coverage attempt failed, including symlink EPERM failures; no aggregate coverage pass is claimed. Independent GPT review, fresh native/public QA, normal CI/coverage and final review are still required. Preserve the original failing probes and author report. No deployment, issue closure or owner acceptance is implied.

# D177 — Complete the real #363 SDK path through the managed patch

The owner delegated blocker decisions for this batch, with explanations and rejected alternatives for consolidated owner review. Select a narrow extension of #363 to the already-managed, pinned `@openai/codex-sdk@0.160.0` patch. Retain its existing windowsHide change. Shorten only the SDK output-schema temporary-directory prefix from `codex-output-schema-` to `gg-schema-`, preserving native mkdtemp exclusive creation, randomness, permissions, schema enforcement, error behavior and cleanup. Record this dependency decision in an ADR and synchronize the patch hash in the lockfile through pnpm; do not change package versions or other dependencies.

Why: independent native Windows QA at adapter candidate 76beeb0f established that the new 249-character adapter scratch is created under a 226-character TEMP root, but the real SDK then fails its own 253-character mkdtemp template before any turn. A short-root control completes and its harmless CLI actually reads the generated schema. The SDK offers no public host temp-root/schema-file override; child env options do not affect its host allocation. This is a sequential blocker to the same reported call, not an unrelated feature.

The shorter SDK prefix should produce a 243-character directory and a 255-character schema file under the exact reported root. Those are predictions, not test results. Verify them through the actual installed patched SDK and native child process, with short-root success and unchanged schema content/cleanup, failing uncorrected SDK counterfactual, failure/abort cleanup and preservation of unrelated paths. Keep the adapter's bounded exclusive mkdir fix and its existing independent allocator evidence. Correct the inaccurate four-retries wording to four attempts (three retries). Do not promise arbitrary Windows long-path support.

Alternatives declined: close the issue on a fake-harness success and document the immediate SDK blocker (would leave the real reported call broken); process-global TEMP mutation or runtime monkeypatch (unsafe concurrency and private behavior); remove outputSchema (loses the contract); introduce a replacement SDK/executor or version upgrade without evidence (larger unrelated surface); duplicate a custom random allocator inside the vendor patch (unnecessary when shortening the existing native mkdtemp prefix satisfies this bounded path).

The original SDK-boundary driver has 0 PASS/2 FAIL because it wrongly counted tsx caches as product residue. Its saved-state readback separately proves the actual short success/long failure and owned scratch cleanup. Preserve both original results and corrected interpretation; no retry-to-green substitution. Manifest: 49b577d1a6776ad8c0cd6ca429b5eeec9e70bd56984b03d738c88c4d6c552bc3.

The existing Claude review remains CHANGES_REQUIRED until a targeted actual Claude re-review of the fix. Independent real-SDK/native QA, unchanged coverage/license/audit gates, current-head/current-target CI and final designated Astra review remain required. No issue closure, owner acceptance, deployment or broader SDK observability/classification policy change is implied.
